label: Thomas Aquinas, In octo libros Physicorum…: Whatever both moves and is moved moves as an…
locator: VIII, lect. 9 n. 1044: whatever “moves and is moved” has the character of an instrument
interpretation: In the second, 'probable' argument that not every mover is moved, Aquinas expounds: of mobile, mover and instrument, the instrument both moves and is moved, 'For this reason, whatever "moves and is moved" has the character of an instrument.' Read as the same proposition as SCG I.13 [15]: being a moved mover suffices for moving as an instrument. Aquinas presents the surrounding argument as probable, not necessary, so the claim records a commitment of the exposition, not a demonstrated premise. Basis: the English translation named in the passage manifest; a candidate for upgrade once a pinned Latin witness exists, and never a ground for overriding a reading of the Leonine/SCTA Latin.
